messages.author: 425d8918bd154a2b
messages.subject: estimating a bianry outcome
parts:
Hi,

I have a latent outcome measured by a single binary item (0,1). When I use the ordered="x" function, I get this error and SE is not calculated:
Warning messages:
1: In lav_data_full(data = data, group = group, cluster = cluster,  :
  lavaan WARNING: some observed variances are (at least) a factor 1000 times larger than others; use varTable(fit) to investigate
2: In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  :
  lavaan WARNING:
    Could not compute standard errors! The information matrix could
    not be inverted. This may be a symptom that the model is not
    identified.
3: In lav_test_satorra_bentler(lavobject = NULL, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  : 
  lavaan WARNING: could not invert information matrix needed for robust test statistic 

However, when DO NOT use the ordered function in cfa(), I get this error but it calculates SE and everything: 
Warning messages:
1: In lav_options_set(opt) :
  lavaan WARNING: estimator “WLSMV” is not recommended for continuous data.
		  Did you forget to set the ordered= argument?
2: In lav_data_full(data = data, group = group, cluster = cluster,  :
  lavaan WARNING: some observed variances are (at least) a factor 1000 times larger than others; use varTable(fit) to investigate
3: In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  :
  lavaan WARNING:
    The variance-covariance matrix of the estimated parameters (vcov)
    does not appear to be positive definite! The smallest eigenvalue
    (= 3.366956e-20) is close to zero. This may be a symptom that the 
    model is not identified. 

What should I do?

Thanks!

parts:
Greetings,
the problem is related to the variance of some of your variables (at least one of them has very large variance) and should multiply it to a fraction (for example 1/100 to solve the error). Of course it is better to check the variance of all variables than decide about what i sead. HTH

I did not run when I used ordinal outside of the lavaan too. This code works despite the warning messages because I did not specify the outcome factor as an ordinal
fit_mediation_model <- sem(mediational_model_1, data = data, meanstructure=TRUE, estimator = "WLSMV") # Delta method 
Warning messages:
1: In lav_options_set(opt) :
  lavaan WARNING: estimator “WLSMV” is not recommended for continuous data.
		  Did you forget to set the ordered= argument?

  lavaan WARNING: some observed variances are (at least) a factor 1000 times larger than others; use varTable(fit) to investigate

    The variance-covariance matrix of the estimated parameters (vcov)
    does not appear to be positive definite! The smallest eigenvalue
    (= -9.275013e-20) is smaller than zero. This may be a symptom that
    the model is not identified.


However, when I used the following code I get the error and I get NA for SE:
